we have successfully used MALDI-MS for direct analysis of lipid metabolism and identified differences in EPA incorporation into phospholipid and cPLA2 expression in two human NSCLC cell lines that could contribute to their different responses to EPA treatment.

the identification of biomarkers of cancer cell metabolism and their potential use as diagnostic and therapeutic targets.
the development of new analytical techniques for cancer biomarker discovery.

the use of MALDI MS for the identification of metabolites in cancer cell lines, and the use of these metabolites to understand cancer biology and to develop biomarkers for the diagnosis and treatment of cancer.

the MALDI-TOF-MS method is very sensitive, reproducible and can provide information about the molecular composition of the lipidome.

this work has successfully demonstrated that direct sample analysis by MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry has the potential for use as a rapid and sensitive tool for identifying biomarkers that may play a key role in regulating the metabolism of omega 3 fatty acids and their potential therapeutic effects.

the MALDI-TOF-MS is capable of identifying differences in lipid metabolism that may contribute to the differential response of cancer cells to omega-3 fatty-acid treatment.

direct sample analysis by MALDI mass spectrometry is a useful approach to identify the biomarker candidates for cancer prevention.
